definitions.explanation: The line along a beach where waves wash up onto the sand. The boundary between water and shore that shifts with each wave.

examples.japanese: {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}を{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked along the water's edge.

examples.japanese: {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}で{貝殻|かいがら}を{拾|ひろ}った。
examples.english: I picked up seashells at the water's edge.

examples.japanese: {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れの{波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}に{二人|ふたり}の{足跡|あしあと}が{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.english: Two sets of footprints remained at the water's edge in the twilight.

notes:
An evocative word that paints a vivid picture of the beach. It specifically refers to the dynamic zone where waves break and wash onto shore — not just any part of the beach. Common in literary descriptions and travel writing.

FORMS:
{波打|なみう}つ (waves breaking) + {際|ぎわ} (edge, boundary)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}を{歩|ある}く: to walk along the water's edge
- {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}で{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play at the water's edge
- {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}に{打|う}ち{上|あ}げられる: to wash up on the shore
- {波打|なみう}ち{際|ぎわ}の{砂|すな}: sand at the water's edge

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {浜辺|はまべ}: beach, seashore — the whole sandy area, not just the water line
- {水際|みずぎわ}: water's edge — more general; can refer to any body of water
- {渚|なぎさ}: shore, beach — a more literary and poetic synonym
